help.census: The census groups live objects by the module that defines their type and counts only shallow sizes. Untracked bytes, strings and C-extension buffers may not appear at all, which is why it stays off until you run it.
help.cgroup: The container limit comes from Linux cgroups. When present it is much closer to the real ceiling for AstrBot than whole-host memory percentage.
help.footprint: Footprint = Pss + SwapPss. Pss splits shared pages across the processes that map them, and SwapPss is the part already pushed out to swap. It is much closer to how much RAM plus swap this process really costs, which matters on a 1-2 GB host.
help.import: Import cost is the RSS delta around a plugin's first load and is good for spotting heavy startup dependencies. Shared packages are charged to whoever imported them first, so it is not the plugin's current exclusive usage.
help.retained: Retained size walks gc.get_referents from plugin instances and modules: objects reachable from exactly one plugin count as exclusive, and objects shared by several plugins are split 1/N. It runs under object and time quotas, so it is always a lower bound rather than an exact bill.
help.rss: RSS is the set of pages the kernel currently keeps in RAM. It is the best signal for how close the machine is to pressure, but it excludes swapped-out memory and never tells you which plugin owns those pages.

safety.cheapProbes: Only two probes run continuously: /proc/self/statm and smaps_rollup (about 5 ms per read, cached for 30 s). The reference scan is sliced by a round-robin quota and yields the CPU on a duty cycle, so it never blocks the event loop for long.
safety.keepCensusOff: Leave the object census off by default and run it by hand while investigating, so a large heap is never walked on a timer.
safety.noTracemalloc: This plugin does not use tracemalloc. Tracemalloc records a traceback for every single allocation, which stretched AstrBot plugin loading from 39 seconds to 21 minutes in a real measurement, and that is not acceptable on a small host.
safety.runDeepManually: Run the deep reference scan only during an investigation and accept that it may cause a brief pause.
safety.useRssAlert: On a small host, configure the process RSS threshold and the RSS growth threshold first; they do not depend on per-plugin attribution.
safety.watchSwap: Watch the footprint and the swapped-out figure. Steadily rising swap usually deserves attention before any per-plugin estimate.

help.safetySub: By default this plugin does nothing that slows AstrBot down.
help.sub: Every number states what it actually measures, and what it cannot see.
help.title: What each metric means
help.trend: Trend is the linear slope of recent samples, shown per minute. Process curves (footprint / RSS / swap) are always available; plugin curves appear only once attribution samples exist.

imports.empty: No import records to show; restart to cover more plugins.
imports.packageHint: A shared package is listed under its first importer and is not charged again to later plugins.

metric.blocksSub: Blocks held by the CPython allocator; a leak makes this climb monotonically.
metric.retainedSub: Objects reachable through the reference graph; shared objects split 1/N.
metric.swapSub: Moved to swap or zram by the kernel; touching it again causes a stall.

table.censusHint: The census is a shallow estimate grouped by defining type module. Select a row for import, object-type and graph details.
table.importHint: Import cost only answers how much startup RSS rose while a plugin loaded; it is not current exclusive memory. Retained sizes fill in as the background scan rotates.
table.retainedHint: Retained = bytes owned exclusively by the plugin plus its 1/N share of the objects it shares. It is an amortised estimate, not exact exclusive RSS; click a row for detail.
